Q: What are the primary indicators of cyclone performance and how should they be monitored?

This indicates the speed at which the gas enters the cyclone. [1] Use a pressure differential sensor
to measure the pressure difference between the inlet and outlet of the cyclone. [1] Use a flow meter
or a differential pressure gauge to measure the velocity of the gas entering the cyclone. [1]

Q: What is roping in a cyclone and why is it undesirable?

Roping in a cyclone occurs when the spigot is choked, meaning it is discharging its maximum amount
of solids, and any coarse solids that cannot get out of the spigot are forced into the wrong
direction, out the cyclone overflow. [1] This is undesirable because it reduces the efficiency of
the cyclone, as the greater the water content in the underflow, the more bypassing of fines occurs
in the cyclone. [1]

Q: What should be checked during routine maintenance of a cyclone dust collector?

Afterfilter bags on the Cyclone Dust Collector are semi-permanent and will give you long, efficient
service if you perform routine maintenance. [1] After each day’s operation, shake the filter bag(s)
vigorously to remove the clinging material. [1] If the afterfilter bag has a zipper-closed bottom,
always empty the bag after shaking. [1] For C-Series afterfilters, open slide gates before shaking
bags so dust can fall into drums. [1] Close slide gates after cleaning is completed. [1]

Q: Is it safe to open the inspection door while the cyclone is running?

Protective Interlocking Limit Switch (PLS), the PLS must be interlocked with all electrical
controls." [4]
